etymologies.etymologyHTML: From actor +‎ -ess. Probably formed independently of Middle French actrice.

definitions.definition: A female who performs on the stage or in films. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1972, Neil Young (lyrics and music), “A Man Needs a Maid”, in Harvest:
quote.text: A while ago somewhere I don't know when / I was watchin' a movie with a friend / I fell in love with the actress / She was playin' a part that I could understand

quote.citation: 2010, Peter Corris, Torn Apart, Allen and Unwin, page 88:
quote.text: "I'm an actress -- actor, as we have to say these days."

quote.citation: 2011 January 27, “Not going quietly”, in The Economist:
quote.text: Court documents appear to show that Ian Edmondson, a senior News of the World journalist, had authorised Mr Mulcaire to hack phones belonging to Sienna Miller, an actress.

definitions.definition: (now rare) A female doer or "actor" (in a general sense). [from 16th c.]

quote.citation: 1796, Matthew Lewis, The Monk, Folio Society, published 1985, page 290:
quote.text: My mental anguish, and the dreadful scenes in which I had been an actress, advanced the period of my labour.
